_comment: IAM statements to ADD to the policy behind echo-dev-github-actions before
enable_ui_waf can be set true in envs/dev-uif.tfvars. This file is the
statement text only -- it is NOT applied by any script here, deliberately.
WHY NOT APPLIED HERE: echo-dev-github-actions is SHARED with the live
echo-dev stack, unlike Apicurio's uif-apicurio-dev-deploy-policy, which
serves one stack and so could carry its own fix script
(stacks/apicurio/infrastructure/deploy/uif-apicurio-dev-deploy-policy-fix.sh).
Widening a shared role is not this change's call to make.
EVIDENCE, not inference. aws iam simulate-principal-policy against
arn:aws:iam::283556840805:role/echo-dev-github-actions on 2026-09-22:
implicitDeny  wafv2:CreateWebACL, GetWebACL, UpdateWebACL, DeleteWebACL
implicitDeny  wafv2:CreateIPSet, GetIPSet
implicitDeny  wafv2:GetRuleGroup
implicitDeny  wafv2:PutLoggingConfiguration, TagResource
allowed       wafv2:ListRuleGroups
allowed       logs:CreateLogGroup, PutRetentionPolicy, TagResource
allowed       cloudfront:UpdateDistribution, GetDistribution
So only the wafv2 actions are missing -- the CloudWatch log group and the
distribution update that waf.tf also needs are already granted. Re-run the
simulation before applying this; a role's policies change.
SCOPING. The two owned resource types are scoped to this stack's own ARNs.
CLOUDFRONT-scope WAFv2 ARNs are global/ under us-east-1 regardless of the
origin's region -- that is the ARN shape AWS uses, not a typo. The trailing
/* is the resource id WAF appends; the name is not the whole ARN.
ARN SHAPE CONFIRMED against a real resource in this account rather than
assumed -- `aws wafv2 list-rule-groups --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1`
returns:
arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:283556840805:global/rulegroup/PCMSanctionsRuleGroupCloudFront/75faf7da-d3d7-489c-a0d5-3d61bd78db03
so the id the wildcard below stands in for is real, and the region and the
global/ segment are the live values, not a guess.
UiWafRuleGroupLookup is Resource "*" for ListRuleGroups because the call
carries no resource to scope against, and scoped to the PCM rule group for
GetRuleGroup. That group is Firewall-Manager-seeded and read-only to us --
no create/update/delete on it, by design.
Every action is create/read/update/delete/tag on resources this stack
declares, plus two read-only lookups. Nothing here grants write access to
another stack's web ACL or to the sanctions group itself.
